Charlie and Emily, who are in the same club, got into an argument at a club meeting last week. It's almost time for today's meeting and Charlie hasn't shown up. Michael, a friend from the club, asks Emily why he hasn't shown up. Emily tells him as follows:

"Either he comes or he doesn't."

Choose the most appropriate meaning of the above utterance from the following options.
(A) Emily doesn't care if Charlie comes or not.
(B) Charlie may or may not come.    
(C) Emily decided to apologize to Charlie.
(D) Emily is not a good speaker.
(E) None of the above.
raw_response:
The correct answer is (B) Charlie may or may not come.

The utterance "Either he comes or he doesn't" is a classic example of a rhetorical question, which is a question that is not intended to elicit a response. In this case, Emily is not asking Michael if Charlie will come, but rather stating that Charlie's attendance is uncertain. The phrase is a way of expressing that Charlie's decision to attend is a binary one - he will either come or he won't, but it's not clear which one it will be.
